'''Keith Robert Jennings''' (5 December 1932 – 18 February 2025) was a British [[chemist]] known for his contributions to [[mass spectrometry]].

Jennings died on 18 February 2025, at the age of 92.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Professor Keith Jennings {{!}} News {{!}} BMSS |url=https://www.bmss.org.uk/mediacentre/news/professor-keith-jennings-2/ |access-date=2026-04-06 |website=www.bmss.org.uk}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
* 1956 Ph.D. Queen’s College Oxford

== Research interests ==
* Structural studies on proteins of significant biological interest

== Awards ==
* 1985 [[International Mass Spectrometry Foundation|Thomson Medal for International Service to Mass Spectrometry]]<ref>{{cite journal |last=Maccoll |first=Allan |year=1997 |title=K.R. Jenning - the man and his work |journal=International Journal of Mass Spectrometry and Ion Processes |doi=10.1016/S0168-1176(97)00200-0 |volume=165-166 |pages=xix–xxi|bibcode=1997IJMSI.165D..19M }}</ref>
* 1995 [[American Society for Mass Spectrometry|Distinguished Contribution in Mass Spectrometry Award]]
* 1998 [[Aston Medal]] awarded by the [[British Mass Spectrometry Society]]
* 1998 Field and Franklin Award for Outstanding Achievement in Mass Spectrometry
